title: Describing motion; Projectile motion; Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's second law; Newton's first law and equilibrium
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.6a, D02-1#N.2, D03-1#N.2, K01-1#N.2, D01-1#N.9, D02-1#N.11, D03-1#N.7a, K01-1#N.5, D01-1#N.12, K01-1#N.10, D01-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity, in m s⁻².

items.label: Displacement
items.clue: The change in position: a vector quantity.

items.label: Average speed
items.clue: Whole path length divided by whole time taken: a scalar.

items.label: Mass
items.clue: Amount of matter in an object, in kg; the same everywhere.

questions.stem: A space probe weighs 4905 N on Earth, where g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. It lands on Mars, where g = 3.7 N kg⁻¹. What is the probe's mass on Mars?

options.text: 190 kg
500 kg

questions.explanation: m = W/g on Earth = 500 kg. Mass does not depend on location, so it is still 500 kg on Mars (where it weighs 500 × 3.7 = 1850 N).

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?

A ball has been thrown straight up and is still rising. Air resistance is not negligible; upthrust (the air's small upward push on the ball) is negligible. Which list gives all the forces acting on the ball, and no others?

options.text: Weight downwards and an upward force from the throw
Weight downwards and drag upwards
Weight and drag, both downwards
Weight only

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; drag opposes the velocity, which is upwards, so drag also points down. Both slow the ball.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: Block X (2.0 kg) and block Y (4.0 kg) rest on a frictionless horizontal surface, joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 24 N pulls X away from Y, and both accelerate together. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: System: a = 24 ÷ 6.0 = 4.0 m s⁻². Y alone: the only horizontal force is the tension, T = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 N.

questions.stem: An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.

questions.stem: A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck
